formation.title: The Crown in Rio
formation.text:
On 16 December 1815 Brazil was raised to a kingdom, the equal of Portugal. The crown now sits on the far side of the ocean, and the question the move left open must be answered: does the king in Rio rule a European monarchy with a great domain in the Americas, or an American one with a homeland in Europe?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

modifiers.name: A Crown of Two Shores
modifiers.text: Portugal and Brazil as equal crowns under one king.

modifiers.name: The New World First
modifiers.text: The crown in Rio looks to its own ocean.

advances.name: Brazilwood Monopoly
advances.text: The red dyewood that gave the land its name belongs to the crown. Indigenous workers cut it and barter it for iron tools, and the logs are stacked at the yards for the king's ships.

advances.name: The Mamelucos
advances.text: Sons of Portuguese fathers and Indigenous mothers, speaking the general language rather than Portuguese, the mamelucos lead the Paulista expeditions through forests no army from Europe could cross.

advances.name: The Jesuit Colleges
advances.text: Nobrega's Jesuits came with the first governor in 1549. Their colleges teach in Bahia, Rio, Olinda and Sao Paulo, their villages gather the Indigenous peoples, and their grammar makes Tupi the general language of the colony.

advances.name: The High Court of Bahia
advances.text: By the law of 7 March 1609 a High Court sits in Salvador for the whole State of Brazil. Appeals no longer cross the ocean.

advances.name: The Forts of Guanabara
advances.text: Rio was founded on 1 March 1565 to drive France Antarctique from the bay. The forts of Santa Cruz and Sao Joao face each other across its mouth, and their fire crosses over the channel.

advances.name: The Henriques
advances.text: Henrique Dias raised a regiment of free, freed and enslaved Black men against the Dutch, and fought from Porto Calvo to the recapture of Recife. Until independence every Black battalion in Brazil bore his name.

advances.name: The Brazilian Way of War
advances.text: Against the Dutch the war was fought from ambush, in the forest, the hills and the mangrove. At Guararapes Camarao's Potiguara and Dias's men struck from the flanks of a narrow pass.

event.title: After Guararapes
event.text: On the hills of Guararapes, in 1648 and again in 1649, the Dutch were broken in the pass between the hills and the mangrove by men the colony itself had raised: Camarao's Potiguara on one flank, Henrique Dias's Black regiment on the other. Dias asks the king for the freedom of every enslaved man who served under him, and for his regiment to keep the rights of the white ones. The captains ask for titles and pensions, as Camarao was made Dom.

modifiers.name: Freedom for the Regiment
modifiers.text: The men who fought at Guararapes serve as free men.

modifiers.name: Honours for the Captains
modifiers.text: Titles and pensions for the officers of the Dutch war.

advances.name: The Galeao Shipyard
advances.text: At the Ponta do Galeao colonial craftsmen and Indigenous workers built the Padre Eterno of light Brazilian woods, launched in December 1663 and called the biggest ship of her time.

advances.name: Luanda from Rio
advances.text: In 1648 a fleet sailed from Rio de Janeiro under Salvador Correia de Sa and took Luanda back from the Dutch. Bahia's tobacco, sewn into leather rolls, is the currency of the Mina coast.

advances.name: The Gold of the Mines
advances.text: Gold on the Rio das Velhas, about 1695. Claims are dealt by the number of slaves a miner brings, men starve in the diggings, and the mint coins what reaches the coast.

event.title: The War of the Emboabas
event.text: The Paulistas found the gold; the newcomers came after it by the thousand from Portugal, Bahia and the coast, and the Paulistas called them emboabas. In 1708 and 1709 the two sides fought for the diggings. The Paulistas want their discoverers' claims confirmed; the governor would open the mines to all who come.

modifiers.name: The Discoverers' Claims
modifiers.text: The Paulistas keep the claims they found, and look west for more.

options.text: Open the mines to all comers

modifiers.name: Mines Open to All
modifiers.text: Anyone may come to the mining country and dig.

advances.name: The Dragoons of Minas
advances.text: A kind of mounted infantry, the dragoon companies guard the registries, patrol the roads of the mines and carry the gold and diamonds down to Rio.

advances.name: The Diamond District
advances.text: From 1734 the district of Serro do Frio is closed and governed from the Intendancy at Tejuco. Stones over twenty carats are the crown's, and in 1760 five years of diamonds are held back from the market.

event.title: The Reserve of Diamonds
event.text: So many stones came out of Serro do Frio that the price of diamonds fell across Europe, and digging was banned from 1735 to 1740 to hold it up. Now the ministers propose to keep five years of Brazil's diamonds off the market in a secret reserve.

modifiers.name: The Diamond Reserve
modifiers.text: Five years of diamonds held back from the market.

advances.name: The Salting Works
advances.text: On the streams of Pelotas the cattle of the southern plains are killed, salted and dried, and the hides stacked in brick stores for the ships.

advances.name: The Road of the Drovers
advances.text: From 1733 droves of mules come up the road from the Rio Grande pastures to Sao Paulo, and Sorocaba's fair sells them to every road of the colony.

advances.name: The High Court of Rio
advances.text: The southern towns offered to pay for a court of their own, and in 1751 the king gave them one in Rio without new taxes.

advances.name: The Baroque of Minas
advances.text: The gold of Minas builds churches, and Aleijadinho, son of a Portuguese master builder and an enslaved African woman, carves their doorways, pulpits and the twelve prophets of Congonhas.

destiny.name: The Crown in Rio
destiny.text: The king rules from the far side of the ocean, and the ministers, judges and treasurers of the crown sit in Rio. A court that crossed the sea must still show it can govern from where it landed. Keep the realm at stability 25 to open the direction chosen at the formation: a crown of two shores, or the New World first.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Crown in Rio
event.text:
The council of state, the high court and the treasury sit in Rio, and the king's decrees cross the ocean to Lisbon instead of coming from it. Portugal's ships still come and go, but the questions they carry are answered here.

A crown is where its king is. Ours is in America.

options.text: The crown is where its king is.

destiny.name: The Garden of Cayenne
destiny.text: In January 1809, at Britain's request, some 700 soldiers and 550 marines sailed from Brazil with one British ship, came ashore at Pointe Mahury and took Cayenne, the capital of French Guiana. The crown that had fled one French army took a French colony, and the trees of its royal spice garden went to Rio in six boxes. Required: own Cayenne, and 50 prestige. Unlocks the Royal Botanical Garden in Rio.

conditions.text: Chose the Crown of Two Shores destiny
Own Cayenne, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 50

event.title: The Spice Trees of Cayenne
event.text:
Cayenne is ours. The landing force came ashore at Pointe Mahury in canoes that were all wrecked on the beach, an armistice followed, and on 14 January 1809 our troops marched into the town; two hundred cannon were surrendered. The colony keeps its French laws under our administration.

The minister Rodrigo de Sousa Coutinho has sent for the trees of its royal spice garden. Nutmeg, clove, breadfruit and avocado are on their way to Rio in six boxes.

options.text: Plant them in the king's garden.

destiny.name: A Court of the Arts
destiny.text: Rio grew from about 43,000 people in 1799 to about 112,000 in 1821. The court gave it a press, a library and a military academy; in 1816 a mission of French artists came to found a school of the arts, and in 1818 a royal museum opened. A European court needs a European capital. Required: Rio grown into a city, the Royal Botanical Garden built there, and 2,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: Rio de Janeiro is ours and has grown into a city
The Royal Botanical Garden stands in Rio de Janeiro
Gold at least 2000

event.title: A Court of the Arts
event.text:
Rio is a court city now. It has a press, a library, a military academy and a garden of the king's own; in 1816 a mission of French artists arrived to found a school of the arts, and in 1818 a royal museum opened its doors. In twenty years the city has grown from some 43,000 people to more than 100,000.

The court must decide where its effort goes next: into Rio itself, the great city of the kingdom, or into the ministers it sends to the other courts.

modifiers.name: The Court's City
modifiers.text: Rio, raised by the court into the great city of the kingdom.

modifiers.name: Ministers Abroad
modifiers.text: The crown's envoys are at every court, and the colonies wait.

destiny.name: A Court Among the Powers
destiny.text: In 1736 the diplomat Luis da Cunha wrote that Portugal could hardly defend itself in Iberia, and that the one real guarantee of its independence lay in the size and wealth of Brazil. A crown ruling both shores from Rio makes that guarantee real once the other powers count it as one of their own. Required: be a great power, with 75 prestige and 3,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: A great power
Prestige at least 75
Gold at least 3000

event.title: A Seat Among the Powers
event.text:
The courts of the world write to Rio as they write to Vienna, Paris and London. A king who left Lisbon ahead of an invading army rules from across the ocean with the standing of a great power.

Da Cunha's prediction has come true. What remains is to decide what the crown makes of its standing: the equal of the old courts in their own diplomacy, or the master of the ocean between its shores.

options.text: Treat with the old courts as their equal.

modifiers.name: Equal of the Old Courts
modifiers.text: The crown in Rio treats with the old courts as their equal.

modifiers.name: The South Atlantic
modifiers.text: The crown's convoys and warships hold the ocean between its shores.

destiny.name: Colonia do Sacramento
destiny.text: On 20 January 1680 Manuel Lobo founded a Portuguese town on the north bank of the River Plate, facing Buenos Aires across the water: a smuggling gate into the trade of the Spanish empire. Spain took it the same year and gave it back, besieged it, took it and gave it back again, and kept it in 1777. Required: own Colonia (Ombu on the map, on the shore below the mouth of the Uruguay), and 1,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: Chose the New World First destiny
Own Ombu, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 1000

event.title: The Colony on the Plate
event.text:
Colonia do Sacramento is ours again, across the river from Buenos Aires, with its walls, its warehouses and its traders who sell to anyone who comes. Every treaty since 1680 has handed it from one crown to the other.

This time the crown means to keep it.

destiny.name: The Captaincy of Mato Grosso
destiny.text: In 1718 or 1719 Pascoal Moreira Cabral found gold on a creek of the Cuiaba, far in the interior, and every flood season canoe convoys left Araritaguaba on the Tiete for the new mines. In 1748 the crown made the far west a captaincy of its own, and in 1750 the Treaty of Madrid drew the border by who held the land. Required: hold Cuiaba (Ikuiapa on the map) and half of Mato Grosso's land, ourselves or through our subjects, and have 2,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: Own Ikuiapa, or a subject owns it
We or our subjects hold half of the land in Mato Grosso that can be owned
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Mines of Cuiaba
event.text:
Since gold was found on a creek of the Cuiaba, the canoe convoys have gone out every March and April from Araritaguaba down the Tiete, up to ten people to a canoe, on the long river road to the mines. In 1748 the crown made the far west a captaincy, and the border with Spain is drawn by who holds the land.

The captaincy can live by its rivers, or by a capital of its own on the Guapore, where the border runs.

modifiers.name: The River Convoys
modifiers.text: Every flood season the canoe convoys leave for the mines.

options.text: Found a capital on the Guapore.

modifiers.name: A Seat on the Guapore
modifiers.text: A capital on the Guapore holds the far west for the crown.

destiny.name: The Cisplatine Province
destiny.text: In 1816 Carlos Frederico Lecor marched into the Banda Oriental with the Royal Volunteer Division, veterans of the wars against Napoleon. He took Montevideo on 20 January 1817 and defeated Jose Artigas in 1820, and in July 1821 a congress he had called voted the land into the kingdom as the Cisplatine province. Required: own the whole Banda Oriental (the province of Guenoa), Montevideo (Charrua on the map) grown into a town, and 75 prestige.

conditions.text: Own entire province is Guenoa
Montevideo (Charrua) is ours and has grown into a town
Prestige at least 75

event.title: The Cisplatine Province
event.text:
The congress Lecor called at Montevideo has voted the Banda Oriental into the kingdom as the Cisplatine province. The war cost the land more than four thousand dead, some six in every hundred of its people.

The province is held by the army that took it, and the crown must choose whom it trusts to keep it.

options.text: Keep Lecor's veterans in the south.

modifiers.name: Lecor's Veterans
modifiers.text: The veterans of the Royal Volunteer Division hold the south.

options.text: Trust the horsemen of Rio Grande.

modifiers.name: The Horse of Rio Grande
modifiers.text: The militia cavalry of Rio Grande rides for the crown.

units.name: Mameluco Woodsmen
units.text: Sons of Portuguese fathers and Indigenous mothers, speaking the general language, who go through the forest for months with Tupi archers. Quick and at home among the trees; lighter than a line regiment in the open.

units.name: The Henriques
units.text: Henrique Dias's regiment of free, freed and enslaved Black men, who fought the Dutch from Porto Calvo to Recife and held the flanks at Guararapes. Steady under fire on broken and wet ground, and they take their losses.

units.name: Minas Dragoons
units.text: A kind of mounted infantry: the dragoon companies of Minas guard the registries, patrol the roads and carry the gold and diamonds to Rio. They ride far and fight on foot; they are no cavalry for the charge.

buildings.name: Regency Palace
buildings.text: The seat of the king's regents in Lisbon, governing the old kingdom for a crown that lives in Rio.

buildings.name: Lisbon Customs House
buildings.text: Brazil's sugar and tobacco clear the customs of Lisbon, whose rules are the model for every customs house of the empire.

buildings.name: Tobacco Board
buildings.text: The Junta da Administracao do Tabaco runs Brazil's tobacco through Lisbon to the kingdom and the islands, and sugar beside it.

buildings.name: Mint of the Brazil Gold
buildings.text: Every ship from Brazil declares its gold at the Lisbon mint: coin, bars, dust and jewels, in hundreds of thousands of declarations.

buildings.name: Commerce Square
buildings.text: The Praca do Comercio opens on the Tagus where the royal palace stood, with the offices of the customs and the port under its arcades.

buildings.name: Brazil Trading House
buildings.text: A merchant house of the town dealing in Brazil's sugar, tobacco and gold. It can grow as far as Lisbon's own trade has grown.

buildings.name: Manioc Clearings
buildings.text: Forest burned and cleared for manioc, the flour of the coast, as the prospectors were ordered to plant it on their way inland. Room and food where no river waters the land.

buildings.name: Brazilwood Yard
buildings.text: Logs of the red dyewood, cut in the forest and stacked for the crown's ships.

where.text: The location's raw material is Lumber

buildings.name: Jesuit College
buildings.text: A college of the Society of Jesus, teaching in Latin and the general language, with mission villages around it.

buildings.name: Forts of Guanabara
buildings.text: Santa Cruz and Sao Joao at the mouth of the bay, their guns crossing fire over the channel.

buildings.name: Galeao Shipyard
buildings.text: The yard at the Ponta do Galeao, where the biggest ship of her time was built of Brazilian wood.

buildings.name: Diamond Intendancy
buildings.text: The crown's office over a closed diamond district: the registries, the guards and the stones that belong to the king.

where.text: The location's raw material is Gems

buildings.name: Charqueada
buildings.text: A salting works: slaughter yard, salt house and brick stores for the hides.

where.text: The location's raw material is Livestock

buildings.name: Royal Botanical Garden
buildings.text: The king's garden at Rio, where the spice trees of the East Indies and of Cayenne, and later the tea of Macau, are made to grow in American soil, and from where new crops go out to the farms of the realm.

effect_groups.label: To the country, when built in the capital

buildings.name: Engenho of Brazil
buildings.text: A sugar estate of Bahia or Pernambuco: cane fields, a mill and a boiling house, worked by enslaved Africans. With the crown in Rio, Brazil is home land, and its estates are built as the crown's own.

where.text: The location's raw material is Sugar

buildings.name: Cotton Estate of Brazil
buildings.text: Cotton fields of Maranhao and Pernambuco, worked by enslaved Africans. With the crown in Rio, Brazil is home land, and its estates are built as the crown's own. The estate raises the cotton harvest of the land.

where.text: The location's raw material is Cotton

buildings.name: Tobacco Farm of Brazil
buildings.text: Tobacco of the Reconcavo of Bahia, the leaf traded on the Mina coast for captives. With the crown in Rio, Brazil is home land, and its farms are built as the crown's own. The farm raises the tobacco harvest of the land.

where.text: The location's raw material is Tobacco

buildings.name: Gold Diggings
buildings.text: The lavras of Minas Gerais: gold washed from rivers and hillsides by enslaved workers. Claims were dealt by the number of slaves a miner brought, and Brazil's gold paid for much of Lisbon's eighteenth century. The diggings raise the gold the land yields.

where.text: The location's raw material is Gold

buildings.name: Trading Post in the Americas
buildings.text: A post of Brazil's merchants on the coasts of North America and the Caribbean. An ordinary overseas trading post cannot stand on the capital's continent; this one can, outside South America, so a crown in Rio can still trade for furs in the north.

list.name: The King's Couples
list.text: By the edict of 1746 the crown sent couples of the Azores with their families to Santa Catarina and, after 1750, to Rio Grande. Each couple was to receive land, tools, food and money on arrival, and in return guard the border. Many waited years for their land. Its funded effect shrinks as Brazil fills: it counts the share of our locations in Brazil still under a quarter of their capacity.

conditions.text: Some of our land in Brazil is still under a quarter of its capacity

list.name: The Directory of the Indians
list.text: Drafted in 1757 by Francisco Xavier de Mendonca Furtado, governor of Grao-Para and Maranhao, and made law for all Brazil on 17 August 1758. Lay directors take the place of the missionaries in the villages, which become towns; the directory rules their farming and trade, shares out their workers among the settlers, and brings in the Portuguese language and mixed marriage. It was revoked in 1798, for the epidemics, the flight into the backlands and the directors' abuses.

conditions.text: Age is Revolutions

list.name: The Boards of Inspection
list.text: Set up in 1751 at the ports of Bahia, Rio, Pernambuco and Maranhao, the boards examine and grade every chest of sugar and roll of tobacco before it sails, to keep the good name of Brazil's crops abroad and to encourage their farming and trade. Left to itself a board becomes one more customs house.

conditions.text: We own land that yields sugar or tobacco

list.name: The Auxiliary Regiments
list.text: Below the paid regular troops stand the auxiliaries, unpaid and armed at their own cost, each horseman with his own horse, and below them the ordenancas, every man over sixteen. In 1766 the king ordered every inhabitant of Minas enlisted. Their officers are chosen from lists the town councils draw up, and the posts carry exemptions and standing, not pay.

list.name: The Intendancy of Police
list.text: Created on 10 May 1808 under the judge Paulo Fernandes Viana, intendant until 1821, the intendancy general of police of the court keeps order in the new capital, sees to its sanitation, and means to make of Rio a new Lisbon.

conditions.text: Our capital is Rio de Janeiro
